subject: MSA + pricing appendix redlines — payee routing & tax evidence
body:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@heliohealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: c.mendez@heliohealth.com, procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — payee routing & tax appendix

Hi Laura,

Attached are HelioHealth's redlines to the MSA and the pricing appendix. High level: procurement needs the invoice/payee to be the HelioHealth USA entity (not their EU affiliate), they'll withhold VAT in their jurisdiction unless we provide evidence of tax residency, and they want net45 rather than net30 on the first two tranches. We've highlighted a couple of clauses (payment routing, invoicing entity, and tax evidence) that block legal sign-off on our side.

Files attached: Helio_Redlines_MSA_20270520.pdf (redlines), Pricing_Appendix_v2.docx (pricing with suggested tranche split).

Happy to walk through these — Sarah (cc) is Helio's finance lead if you want a quick call.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Director, Procurement
HelioHealth

----
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — payee routing & tax appendix

Thanks Sarah — received and reviewed quickly. Internal next steps below.

Ben / Kim / Karthik — tagging you to align legal/commercial/finance:
- Legal: we need a short path to accept Helio's request to invoice the US entity while protecting Redwood for VAT liabilities.
- Finance: confirm whether we can set net45 for the first two tranches and whether that impacts recognition/collections.
- Commercial: suggest alternative wording for the pricing appendix that preserves minimum commit economics if they shift tranche timing.

Proposed approach:
1) Ben, can you propose a redline for the Pricing Appendix that splits the min commit into two linked tranches with the same aggregate ACV but moves invoicing timing?
2) Kim, can you propose a brief clause re: tax evidence e.g., customer to provide 'tax residency certificate' or equivalent within 30 days or risk redirected withholding?
3) Karthik, confirm whether our standard net30->net45 exception needs approval from Accounting and whether this requires PO/credit holds.

If we can agree internally today, I can propose a one-paragraph compromise to Sarah and request a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — payee routing & tax appendix

Laura — high level comments and attached mock language (Pricing_Appendix_v2.docx). Key points:
- We can preserve the customer's economic commitment by splitting their minimum commit into two sub-tranches (Tranche A / Tranche B). Each tranche invoices on signature / 30 days after tranche milestone. Aggregate billing equals the original min commit, so Redwood's revenue protection remains intact.
- For net terms: recommend we propose net45 for Tranche A only (their ask), but keep net30 for subsequent recurring invoices to avoid cashflow strain. If they insist net45 for all invoices we should require a brief credit review and an early-payment fee schedule.
- For invoice routing: accept billing to HelioHealth USA provided the sales order includes an invoice recipient field and we add a 'no change in entity without 30 days' notice' covenant.
- Taxes: suggested clause where customer provides written tax residency or VAT exemption within 30 days; absent evidence they accept gross-up for withheld amounts or provide payment of withholding.

I've attached the appendix with exact redline wording. If that looks good I can circulate to Legal.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: Pricing_Appendix_v2.docx

----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — payee routing & tax appendix

Quick finance note:
- Net45 for the first two tranches is acceptable from a collections perspective if we: (a) require PO upfront for Tranche A and (b) hold Tranche B behind an activation/usage milestone tied to invoice issuance.
- If Helio withholds VAT we prefer a gross-up clause rather than acceptance of net settlement; otherwise revenue recognition and tax reporting becomes complicated across entities.
- Kim (Legal) will need to confirm whether the 'tax residency within 30 days' language is enforceable and what evidence thresholds we should accept (TIN + certificate of residence / withholding statement).

I'll flag Accounting to be ready for a credit check if they push net45 for recurring invoices.

—Karthik
Director, Revenue Ops
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — payee routing & tax appendix

Law has reviewed Helio's redlines in Helio_Redlines_MSA_20270520.pdf. We're comfortable with the invoice-to-US-entity flow provided we add two short protections:
1) A 30-day notice and consent mechanism for any change in invoice recipient or billing entity.
2) A tax-evidence and gross-up fallback: customer must furnish a government-issued certificate of tax residence (or official VAT exemption) within 30 days of invoice; if withheld amounts are applied, customer must either (a) reimburse Redwood for withheld amounts or (b provide proof that Redwood will not be taxed on the net receipts.

I've drafted a one-paragraph MSA addendum and a redline for the Pricing Appendix — both uploaded to the shared drive link above. Key commercial ask: keep the aggregate minimum commit unchanged (Ben's split). Legal prefers net30 for recurring but agrees to net45 on Tranche A only if PO + activation milestone for Tranche B is in place.

If Laura wants, I'll join the call with Helio tomorrow to walk legal points.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

----
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@heliohealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: c.mendez@heliohealth.com, procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form redlines — payee routing & tax appendix

Thanks Laura + team — appreciate the quick review and proposed language.

Helio is generally OK with the Tranche split if you can guarantee aggregate min commit and accept invoicing to our US entity (we will provide the tax residency certificate for the US entity within 30 days of signature). We do still need net45 on Tranche A to align with our internal budget cycles; net30 on recurring is acceptable.

Let's do the 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PDT — invite incoming. I'll bring Carlos (finance) and our legal lead. If you can share the redline version of the appendix and the one-paragraph MSA addendum ahead of that call, we can accelerate sign-off.

Regards,
Sarah Kim
Director, Procurement
HelioHealth

> - Helio_Redlines_MSA_20270520.pdf (redlined MSA)
> - Pricing_Appendix_v2.docx (commercials draft from Ben)
